preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 500000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10^5) representing the number of commands. Subsequent lines are exactly n commands.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and line.split()[0] in {'&', '|', '^'} and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 1023 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each command is a valid operation ('&', '|', or '^') followed by a constant x_i (0 ≤ x_i ≤ 1023).
The first line is a valid non-negative integer representing the number of commands.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda f: (lambda x: eval('x' + ''.join(f))))(commands)(x) == (lambda f: (lambda x: eval('x' + ''.join(f))))(output_commands)(x) for x in range(1024))
postconditions.description: For every input x in [0, 1023], the output program (commands) must produce the same result as the input program (output_commands) when applied to x. The output program is derived from the input commands by minimizing its length to at most 5 while preserving equivalence.
The output program consists of at most 5 commands.

postconditions.expression: all(line in output_commands for line in output_commands) and all(len(line.split()) == 2 and line.split()[0] in {'&', '|', '^'} and 0 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 1023 for line in output_commands)
postconditions.description: The output commands are valid and formatted identically to the input commands.
